# Feature Specification: Inventory Awareness (Read-Only)

**Feature ID:** 013-inventory-awareness
**Status:** Draft (SEED — generated by spec-seed workflow; NOT yet through /speckit-specify)
**Created:** 2026-06-07
**Last Updated:** 2026-06-07
**Owner:** (unassigned)

---

## Overview

> **BLOCKED — NO POS-FACING STOCK CONTRACT EXISTS.**
>
> DP2's `inventory.yaml` is `cookieAuth` / dashboard-scoped. A paired terminal authenticates with
> a device token (`Authorization: Bearer <device_token>`), NOT a `dp2_session` cookie, so the
> terminal CANNOT call the existing inventory surface. The ERPNext live stock view (DP2 spec 019)
> is a Connector→DP2 inbound flow, also not POS-facing. **This feature is blocked until DP2
> publishes a new device-token-authenticated stock-read endpoint.** Implementation planning must
> not begin until that contract is ratified and types are pinned (analogous to 010's §A6 re-pin).

Inventory Awareness gives the cashier a lightweight, read-only signal about a product's
availability at the point of sale — for example an "in stock", "low stock", or "unavailable"
badge on the product card or cart line — without POS-Pulse ever becoming the stock authority or
mutating inventory state.

Architecture anchor (ADR-0001): the ERPNext Item is an accounting identity only. The DP Store
Override is the availability authority. POS-Pulse reflects availability; it never owns it. A
missing or stale availability signal MUST NOT block a sale — the cashier retains full discretion.

The feature consumes whatever POS-facing stock-read contract DP2 publishes (see Dependencies and
Open Questions). POS-Pulse will cache a per-branch availability snapshot locally (SQLite) and
refresh it on a configurable schedule, keeping the terminal functional offline. Data flows
strictly: DP2 → POS-Pulse local cache → renderer (read-only). No write path exists.

---

## User Scenarios & Testing

### Primary User Story

As a cashier scanning or searching for a product, I want to see a clear availability indicator
(e.g. "in stock", "low stock", "out of stock") next to each product so I can set customer
expectations early — without that indicator ever blocking me from completing a sale.

### Acceptance Scenarios

**Scenario 1 — In-stock badge shown on product card**
Given a product whose cached availability status is "in stock"
When the cashier views the product in search results or on the cart line
Then the product displays a green availability badge reading "In Stock"
And no action is blocked or gated on that status

**Scenario 2 — Out-of-stock indicator does not block sale**
Given a product whose cached availability status is "out of stock"
When the cashier adds the product to the cart and proceeds to finalize
Then the sale completes normally
And the terminal logs a staleness/override event (no PII, no card data)
And the cashier sees a non-blocking advisory indicator, not an error

**Scenario 3 — Stale or unavailable cache is surfaced honestly**
Given the local availability cache has not been refreshed within the configured staleness window
(or a refresh has never succeeded)
When the cashier views a product card
Then the availability badge shows a "freshness unknown" or "last updated: <timestamp>" state
And the UI never shows a false "in stock" when data is absent

### Edge Cases

- Product exists in the 009/010 catalogue but has no availability record in the cache → show a
  neutral "availability unknown" state; do not show "in stock" by default.
- Refresh call fails (network error, DP2 unavailable) → retain the last-known cached snapshot;
  surface a staleness warning if the cache age exceeds the configured threshold.
- Product is added to cart while the cache is refreshing → read from the snapshot that was valid
  at add-time; do not block on an in-flight refresh.
- Branch ID mismatch (device re-paired to a different branch) → invalidate and drop the
  availability cache; re-fetch after the new pairing is confirmed.

---

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

**FR-1** The terminal SHALL display a read-only availability indicator (at minimum: in stock / low
stock / out of stock / unknown) on product search results and cart line items.

**FR-2** The availability indicator SHALL be sourced from a local SQLite cache populated by the
DP2 POS-facing stock-read contract (see Dependencies). POS-Pulse SHALL NOT call ERPNext directly.

**FR-3** The terminal SHALL refresh the availability cache from DP2 on a configurable schedule
(default interval TBD pending the contract; expected: minutes-to-hours, not sub-minute).

**FR-4** A stale or absent cache entry SHALL display an explicit "freshness unknown" or staleness
indicator rather than a default "in stock" assumption.

**FR-5** An out-of-stock or unavailable indicator SHALL NEVER block, prevent, or require
confirmation before a sale is completed. It is advisory only.

**FR-6** POS-Pulse SHALL never write to, adjust, or mutate stock or inventory state. The data
flow is read-only in both directions (terminal never sends stock mutations to DP2 or ERPNext).

**FR-7** The availability cache SHALL be scoped to the authenticated branch (`branch_id`). Data
from another branch MUST NOT be shown and MUST be purged on branch change.

**FR-8** Refresh of the availability cache SHALL authenticate with the device token
(`Authorization: Bearer <device_token>`), consistent with the terminal pairing model.

**FR-9** Availability data SHALL never include PII, card data, or operator credentials. Cache
rows and refresh logs must pass the same redaction constraints as the rest of the terminal.

**FR-10** The UI SHALL surface a manual "Refresh availability" action (analogous to
`catalogue:refresh`) so a cashier can trigger an out-of-cycle pull when they suspect stale data.

### Non-Functional Requirements

**NFR-1** The availability badge render MUST NOT add perceptible latency to product search or
cart-line display. Badge data is read from the local SQLite cache synchronously on the main
process; no network call on the hot path.

**NFR-2** A full availability refresh for a typical branch catalogue (≤ 10,000 SKUs) MUST
complete within 30 seconds on target hardware (LENOVO 82K2 / Ryzen 7 5800H) on a stable
connection. This target is provisional pending the contract shape.

**NFR-3** The terminal MUST remain fully operational (sales, search, barcode lookup) when the
availability cache is absent, stale, or being refreshed.

---

## Success Criteria

**SC-1** A cashier can see an availability badge on every product card and cart line item that has
a cache entry; products without a cache entry show "availability unknown" — never a false positive.

**SC-2** An out-of-stock badge does not prevent any sale from completing (zero blocking events in
QA regression across all finalization paths).

**SC-3** A staleness indicator appears when the cache is older than the configured threshold,
giving the cashier actionable awareness without blocking them.

**SC-4** The feature passes the §A4 bridge-security review (all IPC channels authenticated,
sandboxed, no upward-of-bridge calls) before any renderer wiring merges.

**SC-5** No stock mutation reaches DP2 or ERPNext from POS-Pulse at any point in the feature
implementation or test suite.

---

## Key Entities

- **AvailabilityRecord** — local cache row: `(product_id, branch_id, status, quantity_hint?,
  refreshed_at, source_contract_version)`. Field names are provisional; final shape depends on
  the DP2 contract.
- **AvailabilityStatus** — enum: `IN_STOCK | LOW_STOCK | OUT_OF_STOCK | UNKNOWN`. `UNKNOWN` is
  the safe default when no cache entry exists or the cache is expired beyond the hard staleness
  limit.
- **AvailabilitySyncState** — metadata row (analogous to 010's `catalogue_sync_state`): last
  successful refresh timestamp, last attempt timestamp, error count, branch_id.
- **DP2 POS Stock-Read Contract** — the not-yet-published device-token-authenticated endpoint.
  Named here as a placeholder; actual path, response shape, and pagination model are unknown.

---

## Assumptions

- **A1** — DP2 will publish a device-token-authenticated stock-read endpoint before this feature
  is planned. This spec makes no assumptions about its URL, response schema, or pagination.
- **A2** — Availability authority is the DP Store Override layer, NOT the raw ERPNext bin ledger.
  POS-Pulse will reflect whatever DP2 exposes; it will not attempt to reconcile ERPNext ledger
  data independently.
- **A3** — Availability data is branch-scoped. A terminal only needs the snapshot for its own
  `branch_id`.
- **A4** — "Never blocks sale" is a hard product constraint, not a configurable flag. No setting
  will ever gate sale completion on availability status.
- **A5** — The quantity hint (if any) exposed by the contract is informational only. POS-Pulse
  will not compute derived stock positions or trigger replenishment signals.

---

## Out of Scope

- Any write path to inventory (stock adjustments, receiving, returns-driven restock).
- POS-Pulse computing or owning stock positions (quantity on hand, reorder points).
- ERPNext direct calls of any kind.
- Real-time (sub-second) stock streaming or websocket push. Cache-refresh polling only.
- Inventory reservation at cart-add time (optimistic locking / hold logic).
- Replenishment, purchase order, or warehouse management workflows.
- Surfacing ERPNext bin ledger detail rows in the POS UI.
- Multi-branch availability comparison.
- VAT, fiscal, or receipt integration related to stock.

---

## Dependencies

> **PRIMARY BLOCKER (unresolved):** A new DP2 device-token-authenticated stock-read contract
> must be designed, reviewed, and deployed before this feature can be planned or implemented.
> The existing `inventory.yaml` is `cookieAuth` / dashboard-scoped and is inaccessible to a
> paired terminal. No workaround exists within the current architecture.

- **DP2 POS Stock-Read Contract** (BLOCKED — does not exist) — the missing POS-facing endpoint.
  Analogous to the 010 §A6 re-pin dependency. Implementation is gated on this contract being
  ratified and types pinned in `src/shared/api-types.ts`.
- **Feature 002 — Terminal Pairing** — device token (`Authorization: Bearer <device_token>`) must
  be available for the refresh request. Already shipped.
- **Feature 009 — Product Search & Barcode Lookup** — provides the `product_id` namespace that
  availability records must join against. Already shipped.
- **Feature 010 — Catalog Read-Down Consumption** — provides the local `products` table and the
  SQLite migration runner pattern. Partially shipped (live-fetch leg gated on #349).
- **DP2 issue tracking the new stock-read contract** — to be filed; this feature must reference
  that issue as its §A6 equivalent.

## Open Questions

**[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: What is the shape of the new DP2 device-token-authenticated stock-read
contract?]** Specifically: URL path, authentication header, response schema (status enum values,
quantity fields, pagination), and rate-limit / throttling constraints. Nothing in this spec can be
finalized until this contract is published and reviewed. The `inventory.yaml` dashboard surface
is NOT usable by a paired terminal.

**[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: What is the intended refresh cadence and staleness policy?]** Should the
terminal treat availability as "soft real-time" (refresh every few minutes) or "session-fresh"
(refresh once per operator session or on manual trigger only)? The answer affects cache schema
design, battery/network cost on target hardware, and the staleness UX thresholds in NFR-2.

**[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: Should the availability badge surface a quantity hint (e.g. "3 left") or
only a categorical status (in stock / low / out)?]** If the contract exposes a quantity, the
display and redaction policy need to be defined (quantities could be commercially sensitive). A
categorical-only surface is architecturally simpler and easier to keep non-blocking.
